data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An append-only event log requires writers to be safe (capable of deduplication) rather than purely idempotent because a naive append operation executed twice violates idempotency (yielding two entries instead of one), whereas a 'safe to retry' operation uses deterministic identifiers or content-addressable hashes to prevent duplicate side effects during at-least-once delivery.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The underlying transport guarantees exactly-once delivery, making safe retries unnecessary.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The system expects duplicate events in the log and handles idempotency at the downstream consumer level rather than at the writer level.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Idempotency strictly means that applying an operation multiple times has the same effect as applying it once (f(f(x)) = f(x)). A blind append-only write does not satisfy this, as retrying the append creates duplicate events.
